title: One row per sensor tag
prompt: The placement team counts readings by tag, so they want the tags as rows. Write `solve(sensor_readings)` so it returns `reading_id`, `device_id`, `reading_date` (the day of `event_time`) and `tag`, with one row for each tag of each reading.
rules: One row per item of `payload.tags`. A reading with three tags gives three rows.
`reading_date` is the date of `event_time` (when the sensor measured), not of `arrival_time`.
A reading with no tags, or no payload, gives no rows. Keep repeats: a reading delivered twice gives its rows twice.
Return only `reading_id`, `device_id`, `reading_date` and `tag`, in that order.
hints: `F.explode` turns an array into one row per item, copying the other columns you select.
The array is inside the struct: `F.explode("payload.tags")`. `F.to_date` gives the day of a timestamp.
`F.explode` can sit in the same `select` as ordinary columns and the date. Give both new columns their names with `alias`.
starter:
from pyspark.sql import functions as F


def solve(sensor_readings):
    # Return one row per tag of each reading.
    return sensor_readings
